                })\\n                            .collect();\\n                        div().flex().flex_row().children(cells)\\n                    }\\n                })\\n                .collect();\",\"originalFile\":\"//! GPUI window-opening entry point — [`run`] opens a native\\n//! GPUI window, constructs an [`EditorView`], drives the event\\n//! loop, and tears down cleanly on `editor.should_quit`.\\n//!\\n//! Phase 5.9 migration: the body used to live in\\n//! `src/bin/lattice_gpui.rs`. Moving it into the lib (behind\\n//! the `window` Cargo feature) lets `lattice-cli` route through\\n//! a single `lattice --gpu` flag without duplicating the\\n//! window setup. The `lattice-gpui` binary becomes a thin\\n//! shim: tracing init + CLI arg parse + [`run`].\\n//!\\n//! The whole module is `#[cfg(feature = \\\"window\\\")]`-gated by\\n//! `lib.rs`, so `cargo test -p lattice-ui-gpui` on a headless\\n//! host (without display libs) still works — gpui only links\\n//! when the `window` feature is on.\\n//!\\n//! ## Pipeline\\n//!\\n//! 1. [`run`] takes a [`Document`] (path-bearing or empty),\\n//!    constructs `gpui::Application::new()`, and opens a 720×480\\n//!    centered window whose root element is an [`EditorView`].\\n//! 2. [`EditorView::new`] calls `GpuiApp::new(document)`, which\\n//!    delegates to [`lattice_host::editor::Editor::boot`] for the\\n//!    full renderer-neutral setup (LSP, command + mode + snippet\\n//!    registries, syntax handle, buffer registry, persistent\\n//!    config, picker registry, ...).\\n//! 3. After `cx.open_window` returns, we do a second\\n//!    `window.update(cx, ...)` to focus the editor view + call\\n//!    `cx.activate(true)`. The focus call HAS to happen after\\n//!    `open_window` -- calling it inside the builder closure\\n//!    runs before gpui's focus tree is fully initialised and is\\n//!    silently dropped. The pattern matches gpui's\\n//!    `examples/input.rs`.\\n//! 4. Keystrokes flow `on_key_down` → `dispatch_keystroke` →\\n//!    `editor.dispatch` → renderer signals + next-action chain;\\n//!    `cx.notify()` schedules a repaint; `cx.stop_propagation()`\\n//!    prevents the platform default action map from claiming the\\n//!    chord.\\n//! 5. `editor.should_quit` → `cx.quit()` tears the application\\n//!    down.\\n//!\\n//! ## What renders today\\n//!\\n//! - **Document area**: per-character cells laid out under\\n//!   `flex_row` lines + `flex_col` columns on a monospace font,\\n//!   with a left-side line-number gutter (5.8.D). Syntax\\n//!   highlights (5.8.A) color each span via the Catppuccin Mocha\\n//!   palette when an `editor.syntax` handle exists.\\n//! - **Vim-style cursor**: three shapes via [`CursorShape`]\\n//!   (block / bar / underline) based on `editor.modal` (5.7.B.11).\\n//! - **Status line / minibuffer**: shows\\n//!   `<MODAL>   <path>[+]   L:<n>  C:<n>` (5.8.B), or the\\n//!   in-progress `:command` / `/pattern` line when in Command /\\n//!   Search modes (5.8.C).\\n//! - **DisplayBuffer popup** (5.7.B.10): centered overlay for\\n//!   `:ls`, `:describe-buffer`, etc. Esc dismisses.\\n//! - **Picker overlay** (5.8.E): for `:picker files`,\\n//!   `:picker commands`.\\n//! - **Insert-mode completion popup** (5.8.F): top-right\\n//!   anchored panel.\\n\\nuse anyhow::{Context as _, Result};\\nuse gpui::{\\n    App, AppContext, Application, Bounds, Context, FocusHandle, Focusable, InteractiveElement,\\n    IntoElement, KeyDownEvent, ParentElement, Render, SharedString, Styled, TextRun, Window,\\n    WindowBounds, WindowOptions, div, font, px, rgb, size,\\n};\\nuse lattice_core::Document;\\nuse lattice_core::ui::pane::{PaneNode, PaneState};\\nuse lattice_grammar::ModalState;\\nuse lattice_host::cursor_shape::CursorShape;\\nuse lattice_host::per_buffer_cache::PerBufferCacheExt;\\nuse lattice_syntax::Style as SyntaxStyle;\\n\\nuse crate::{GpuiApp, GpuiTheme};\\n\\n// Phase 5.8.AF.5 / Slice X3.full.2: `CellStyle` + `run_to_cell`\\n// (per-cell styled-Div construction) deleted -- replaced by the\\n// shaping-layer logic in `crate::editor_element::build_text_runs`.\\n// `syntax_color` + `style_at` are kept because the popup-overlay\\n// renderer below still walks chars and emits one Div per cell.\\n// Slice X3.full.3 absorbs the popup into a shaped-line path; at\\n// that point these helpers move into `editor_element` too.\\n\\n/// Adapter: host-canonical [`Theme::syntax_style`] -> packed 24-bit\\n/// `0xRRGGBB`. The fallback when `fg` is unset is the Catppuccin Text\\n/// (`0xcdd6f4`) — matches what `SyntaxStyle::Default` resolves to\\n/// and what `EditorElement` paints on un-spanned bytes.\\nfn syntax_color(style: SyntaxStyle) -> u32 {\\n    let host_default = lattice_host::ui::theme::Theme::default();\\n    let host_style = host_default.syntax_style(style);\\n    host_style\\n        .fg\\n        .map(|c| c.to_rgb_u32(0xcdd6f4))\\n        .unwrap_or(0xcdd6f4)\\n}\\n\\n/// Walk `spans` (one entry per line) and find the `Style` that\\n/// covers `byte`.\\nfn style_at(spans: &[lattice_syntax::StyledSpan], byte: usize) -> SyntaxStyle {\\n    for span in spans {\\n        if byte >= span.start && byte < span.end {\\n            return span.style;\\n        }\\n    }\\n    SyntaxStyle::Default\\n}\\n\\n/// Reads the typed `picker.display` option and returns `true` iff\\n/// the user wants the vertico-style minibuffer layout (default).\\n/// Unknown / missing values fall back to the design default rather\\n/// than panicking -- the validator already gates set-time. `HorizontalSplit { top, bottom }` divides HEIGHT between\\n///   children; both get the full width.\\n/// - `VerticalSplit { left, right }` divides WIDTH between\\n///   children; both get the full height.\\n/// - per_leaf_v_chrome_px).max(0.0);\\n            let usable_w = (available_w_px - per_leaf_h_chrome_px).max(0.0);\\n            let rows = (usable_h / row_px).floor().max(1.0) as u32;\\n            let cols = (usable_w / col_px).floor().max(1.0) as u32;\\n            out.push((*idx, rows, cols));\\n        }\\n        PaneNode::HorizontalSplit { top, bottom, ratio } => {\\n            // Issue #28: ratio-aware split (0.5 = even).\\n            let top_h = available_h_px * *ratio;\\n            let bot_h = available_h_px - top_h;\\n            collect_pane_geometries(\\n                top,\\n                available_w_px,\\n                top_h,\\n                per_leaf_v_chrome_px,\\n                per_leaf_h_chrome_px,\\n                row_px,\\n                col_px,\\n                out,\\n            );\\n            collect_pane_geometries(\\n                bottom,\\n                available_w_px,\\n                bot_h,\\n                per_leaf_v_chrome_px,\\n                per_leaf_h_chrome_px,\\n                row_px,\\n                col_px,\\n                out,\\n            );\\n        }\\n        PaneNode::VerticalSplit { left, right, ratio } => {\\n            let left_w = available_w_px * *ratio;\\n            let right_w = available_w_px - left_w;\\n            collect_pane_geometries(\\n                left,\\n                left_w,\\n                available_h_px,\\n                per_leaf_v_chrome_px,\\n                per_leaf_h_chrome_px,\\n                row_px,\\n                col_px,\\n                out,\\n            );\\n            collect_pane_geometries(\\n                right,\\n                right_w,\\n                available_h_px,\\n                per_leaf_v_chrome_px,\\n                per_leaf_h_chrome_px,\\n                row_px,\\n                col_px,\\n                out,\\n            );\\n        }\\n    }\\n}\\n\\nfn picker_display_is_minibuffer(app: &GpuiApp) -> bool {\\n    // Slice 3c.final.B.10: typed-options registry via published\\n    // `options()` sub-state — wait-free Arc clone.\\n    app.options()\\n        .config\\n        .get_typed::<lattice_config::core_options::PickerDisplay>()\\n        .map(|s| s.as_str() != \\\"popup\\\")\\n        .unwrap_or(true)\\n}\\n\\n/// Slice `3c.unify.gpui-annotation-render`: shared candidate-row\\n/// builder for the picker (minibuffer + overlay) and cmdline-\\n/// completion (minibuffer + overlay) surfaces. Replaces four\\n/// near-identical inline row builders.\\n///\\n/// Layout: `[display + match highlights]   [annotations]` —\\n/// candidate text on the left, annotations right-aligned in a\\n/// dimmer colour. Matches the TUI peer's `candidate_to_line`\\n/// shape. Empty `annotations` → no right column (no extra width\\n/// reserved, no two-space gap).\\n///\\n/// `padded`: when true, applies `px_2()` for the strip variants\\n/// that need horizontal padding. The overlay variants paint\\n/// inside a bordered container that already has its own padding.\\nfn paint_candidate_row(\\n    cand: &lattice_completion::RenderedCandidate,\\n    selected: bool,\\n    theme: &GpuiTheme,\\n    padded: bool,\\n) -> gpui::Div {\\n    // Issue #35 (2026-05-22): match highlight now uses\\n    // `picker_match_highlight` (Catppuccin peach by default,\\n    // distinct from `foreground`). Previously used\\n    // `cursor_background` which is identical to `foreground`\\n    // in the Catppuccin Mocha defaults — match highlights\\n    // were invisible.\\n    let match_hl_fg = rgb(theme.picker_match_highlight);\\n    let row_bg = if selected {\\n        Some(rgb(theme.status_background))\\n    } else {\\n        None\\n    };\\n    let row_fg = if selected {\\n        rgb(theme.status_foreground)\\n    } else {\\n        rgb(theme.foreground)\\n    };\\n    // Marginalia (kind glyph on the left + annotations on the\\n    // right) uses `picker_marginalia_fg`. The selected-row\\n    // case bumps to a slightly brighter shade so it stays\\n    // legible against the status background.\\n    let marginalia_fg = if selected {\\n        rgb(theme.foreground)\\n    } else {\\n        rgb(theme.picker_marginalia_fg)\\n    };\\n    let display = &cand.raw.display;\\n\\n    // Left side: display text with optional per-char match\\n    // highlighting. Fast path: no match ranges → single child\\n    // (empty-query \\\"show all\\\" hits this every row).\\n    let display_div: gpui::Div = if cand.match_ranges.is_empty() {\\n        div().child(display.clone()).text_color(row_fg)\\n    } else {\\n        let in_match = |byte_idx: usize| -> bool {\\n            cand.match_ranges\\n                .iter()\\n                .any(|r| byte_idx >= r.start && byte_idx < r.end)\\n        };\\n        let cells: Vec<gpui::Div> = display\\n            .char_indices()\\n            .map(|(byte_idx, c)| {\\n                let cell = div().child(c.to_string());\\n                if in_match(byte_idx) {\\n                    cell.text_color(match_hl_fg)\\n                } else {\\n                    cell.text_color(row_fg)\\n                }\\n            })\\n            .collect();\\n        div().flex().flex_row().children(cells)\\n    };\\n\\n    // Issue #35-followup (2026-05-22): user reported the\\n    // marginalia floated to the far-right edge in maximized\\n    // windows. Previously `justify_between().w_full()` pushed\\n    // annotations across the whole screen; now annotations\\n    // sit right after the display text with a small gap.\\n    // The row's `w_full` is kept ONLY so the selected-row bg\\n    // fills the strip; child layout is natural (no\\n    // justify_between).\\n    let annotation_text = cand.annotations.join(\\\"  \\\");\\n    let mut row = div().flex().flex_row().w_full();\\n    if padded {\\n        row = row.px_2();\\n    }\\n    // Issue #35 (2026-05-22): left-margin kind glyph (one\\n    // ASCII char) so the user can scan candidates by kind\\n    // (`f` = file, `b` = buffer, `:` = command, etc.). Sits\\n    // in `marginalia_fg` so it doesn't compete with the\\n    // display text.\\n    let kind_glyph = format!(\\\"{} \\\", cand.raw.kind.glyph());\\n    row = row\\n        .child(div().text_color(marginalia_fg).child(kind_glyph))\\n        .child(display_div);\\n    if !annotation_text.is_empty() {\\n        // 2-space gap after the display text, then the\\n        // annotation.   <type>discovery</type>
  <title>Hover request spawns LSP runtime task sending HoverOutcome through unbounded channel</title>
  <subtitle>do_request_hover creates channel and token, spawns async task calling server handle.hover sending response to pending_hover_rx</subtitle>
  <facts>
    <fact>do_request_hover at dispatch.rs line 7502 creates unbounded_channel for HoverOutcome communication</fact>
    <fact>CancellationToken created at line 7503 stored as pending_hover_token for request cancellation on cursor motion</fact>
    <fact>pending_hover_rx receiver stored on editor at line 7504 for drain_pending_hover to poll</fact>
    <fact>Async task spawned at line 7511 via spawn_on_lsp_runtime calls handle.hover(params, token)</fact>
    <fact>On successful hover response with non-empty body, task sends HoverOutcome::Body(body) via tx at line 7561</fact>
    <fact>hover_contents_to_markdown converts LSP Hover contents to markdown string before sending</fact>
  </facts>
  <narrative>The hover request mechanism creates an unbounded channel and cancellation token when do_request_hover is called. The receiver and token are stored on the editor as pending_hover_rx and pending_hover_token. An async task is spawned on the LSP runtime that calls the server's hover method with the cursor position converted to LSP coordinates. When the server responds with hover content, the task converts it to markdown and sends HoverOutcome::Body through the channel. The drain_pending_hover method (called from dispatch_action's tail) polls this receiver and emits DisplayBuffer signals for non-empty responses. If the cursor moves before the response arrives, the cancellation token is used to abort the request, preventing stale popups from appearing.</narrative>

  <type>discovery</type>
  <title>Hover outcomes distinguish between NoBody, NoServers, and successful Body responses</title>
  <subtitle>Three HoverOutcome variants handle empty responses, missing servers, and successful content differently in drain logic</subtitle>

  <narrative>The hover request system distinguishes three outcome scenarios through the HoverOutcome enum. When servers respond with non-empty content, HoverOutcome::Body is sent with the markdown string. If servers are attached but none return content after trying all of them, HoverOutcome::NoBody is sent with a servers_tried count. If no servers are attached to the buffer's URI, HoverOutcome::NoServers is sent immediately. The drain_pending_hover method consumes these outcomes and either displays a popup for Body or echoes informational messages for NoBody and NoServers. This design provides clear feedback about why hover information isn't available, helping users distinguish between configuration issues and symbol resolution failures.</narrative>

<observation>
  <type>discovery</type>
  <title>ensure_cursor_visible clamps cursor within viewport using scroll and viewport_height</title>
  <subtitle>Cursor visibility maintained by adjusting scroll when cursor moves outside scroll to scroll plus viewport_height range</subtitle>
  <facts>
    <fact>ensure_cursor_visible defined at dispatch.rs line 1812 no-ops when viewport_height is 0 per line 1813</fact>
    <fact>Bottom of viewport calculated as scroll + viewport_height - 1 at line 1819</fact>
    <fact>When cursor exceeds bottom, scroll adjusted to cursor.line + 1 - viewport_height bringing cursor into view at line 1821</fact>
    <fact>viewport_height set via Action::SetViewportHeight at line 860 with max(1) floor</fact>
    <fact>snap_cursor_past_closed_folds at line 9530 handles fold-related cursor adjustments</fact>
  </facts>
  <narrative>The ensure_cursor_visible method maintains cursor visibility by clamping it within the viewport bounds defined by scroll and viewport_height. When viewport_height is zero (uninitialized or headless mode), the method no-ops. Otherwise, it calculates the bottom of the visible range as scroll + viewport_height - 1. If the cursor's line exceeds this bottom boundary, scroll is adjusted to cursor.line + 1 - viewport_height, effectively scrolling the viewport to keep the cursor visible. The viewport_height is set by the renderer through Action::SetViewportHeight and is floored at 1 to prevent division by zero. This design ensures the cursor remains visible after navigation commands without requiring the renderer to manually track scroll adjustments.</narrative>

<observation>
  <type>discovery</type>
  <title>Second K press focuses existing popup via focus_help_popup instead of firing new hover request</title>
  <subtitle>lsp_hover_request checks popup_buffer presence returning early to call focus_help_popup for State A to B transition</subtitle>
  <facts>
    <fact>lsp_hover_request at dispatch.rs line 7460 checks if popup_buffer.is_some() before firing hover request</fact>
    <fact>When popup exists, calls focus_help_popup() at line 7461 and returns immediately at line 7462</fact>
    <fact>First K with no popup creates channel, spawns LSP task, stores receiver at lines 7502-7505</fact>
    <fact>focus_help_popup transitions from State A (unfocused overlay) to State B (focused popup) enabling j/k scrolling</fact>
    <fact>Pending hover token cancelled before new request at line 7468 to abort stale requests</fact>
  </facts>
  <narrative>The lsp_hover_request method handles both initial hover requests and popup focus transitions through a simple guard at line 7460. When a popup already exists (popup_buffer.is_some()), it calls focus_help_popup() and returns early, transitioning from State A (popup visible but unfocused, document still has keyboard focus) to State B (popup focused, j/k scroll the popup). This is the double-K UX: first K requests hover and displays overlay, second K focuses the overlay for scrolling. When no popup exists, the method proceeds to cancel any pending hover token, create a fresh channel, and spawn the LSP request task. This design cleanly separates hover request initiation from popup focus management.</narrative>

  <type>discovery</type>
  <title>CursorAnchored popup positioning uses anchor snapshot and doc_scroll_at_anchor to avoid State B frame jump</title>
  <subtitle>Popup position computed from captured cursor anchor instead of live values preventing popup from following scroll changes</subtitle>
  <facts>
    <fact>CursorAnchored placement at window.rs line 1946 uses popup_substate.anchor captured at popup-open time per line 1958</fact>
    <fact>Falls back to ad.cursor defensively when anchor is None for pre-anchor-field state at line 1958</fact>
    <fact>Uses doc_scroll_at_anchor instead of ad.scroll per comment at line 1960 because ad.scroll becomes popup's scroll in State B</fact>
    <fact>cursor_screen_row computed as anchor.line minus doc_scroll_at_anchor at line 1963</fact>
    <fact>Popup placed below cursor at pane_pad_px plus (cursor_screen_row plus 1.0) times estimated_row_px at line 1972</fact>
    <fact>Comment at line 1961 explicitly states State B causes ad.scroll to be POPUP's scroll causing frame-jump</fact>
  </facts>
  <narrative>The CursorAnchored popup positioning system captures the cursor position and document scroll at popup-open time to prevent position jumping when focus shifts to the popup. In State B (popup focused), the editor's ad.scroll field reflects the popup's scroll position rather than the document's, which would cause the popup to jump on the second K press if positioning used live values. To avoid this, popup_substate stores anchor (cursor snapshot) and doc_scroll_at_anchor (document scroll at open time). The cursor screen row is computed relative to this captured scroll, then the popup is positioned one line-height below to avoid covering the symbol.
